checklist.fact: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, for MoDOT as the beneficiary (Right of Way staff are the users of the tool).
The need: property descriptions for MHTC must be written by metes and bounds and reviewed by a professional land surveyor, and these descriptions are long and tedious to write.
The project goal is to determine the usefulness of AI and ML to develop a "first draft" legal land description using MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would review and edit.
The services are capped at a not-to-exceed price of $175,000.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project assumed to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending February 2, 2026 with the final invoice due.
Proposals for project TR202504 must be emailed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
Questions must be submitted by 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central via the RFP email only; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification.
Property descriptions must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, which the RFP references but does not include.

Core deliverables include a data management plan, a proof-of-concept demonstration of AI writing legal land descriptions, training and a user manual for ROW staff, and draft and final reports; the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.
Web applications must meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility conformance.
No PII may be stored in any database table unless there is a specific business need, and any stored PII requires approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named principal investigator runs the engagement under a work plan MoDOT approves, with a kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024 to confirm scope, schedule and a communications protocol. We hold quarterly status meetings with written minutes, deliver quarterly written progress updates on the last working day of March, June, September and December, and provide monthly e-mail and phone updates to the MoDOT project manager. An interim presentation near the mid-point (by 9/15/2025) reports progress and direction. All activity is coordinated with the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, and we consult MHTC's representative on any administrative concern and keep advice and information available to that Division throughout the term.

component_records.title: Literature review and state-of-practice synthesis
component_records.description: Task 2 delivers a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practice in applying AI/ML to right-of-way work, covering document-generation approaches, accuracy and review workflows, and lessons from comparable deployments. The review is written to feed directly into tool selection and into the draft Synthesis Report, so the client sees the evidence base behind every design choice. Findings are summarized in a form usable in the final report and research summary.

component_records.title: Named LLD development program and IS approval package
component_records.description: Before any proof-of-concept work, we name the specific program used to develop LLDs and submit it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval, including a technology and licensing review package for the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management so no licensing responsibility falls on MoDOT without prior approval. The package documents the approved-technology basis (.NET 6.0+ or .NET Framework 4.8+, MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, C#/JavaScript/CSS/HTML and limited Python), the database platform (Oracle 19C or supported SQL Server), and confirms no PII is stored without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval. Approval is treated as a gating milestone in the schedule.

component_records.title: Browser-based LLD drafting environment
component_records.description: We build and configure the drafting environment as a web application requiring only a modern browser, with no Java Applets or Silverlight, using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API on a supported .NET release and an approved on-premise database. The interface meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508, is tested on the latest IS-approved browsers, and carries no vendor logos or branding where a supported, licensed way to remove them exists. The environment encodes MHTC parameters — metes and bounds descriptions unless the property is taken in its entirety, in which case the last deed of record is reproduced exactly, with specific rights recited where less than fee simple — and produces a first draft for ROW staff to review and edit.

component_records.title: Proof of concept on MoDOT-supplied LLD examples
component_records.description: Task 3a ingests the LLD examples MoDOT provides and uses them as the reference corpus and evaluation set. By 4/25/2025 we demonstrate how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions across a variety of property types, and MoDOT reviews the drafts and returns improvement feedback. We iterate on that feedback, with a professional land surveyor on the team reviewing output against EPG 236.4.6.2 and deed-of-record requirements, and report measured accuracy and edit effort per draft so the client can judge usefulness rather than take it on assertion.

component_records.title: Training, user manual and change support for ROW staff
component_records.description: After the tool is adjusted on the basis of MoDOT feedback, we deliver training to Right of Way staff by 7/25/2025 and supply a user manual for staff reference. Training covers drafting workflow, review and edit of AI-generated text, surveyor review hand-off, and the limits of the tool, and is delivered in sessions scheduled with ROW supervisors. The manual is updated alongside the tool and reissued with the draft and final deliverables so staff always hold a current version.

component_records.title: Data management plan and data handling
component_records.description: We submit a Data Management Plan by 12/4/2024, within two weeks of the 11/15/2024 kick-off, describing anticipated data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan covers the LLD example corpus, training data, model artifacts and evaluation results, and sets retention, access and hand-over rules consistent with MHTC ownership of all data and documents produced.

component_records.title: Reporting, research summary and final presentation
component_records.description: We deliver a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with supporting documentation by 11/3/2025, then the final report detailing every task and finding, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, a presentation for MoDOT staff, and the final user manual by 1/1/2026. Reports follow MoDOT's Publication Guidelines and research summary template, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page. The final invoice is submitted and the contract closes on 2/2/2026.

component_records.title: Price page, budget control and cost reporting
component_records.description: We complete, sign and return the Section (4) Price Page with the proposal, breaking costs into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, and we agree to perform at the quoted fees. The budget is managed to the $175,000 not-to-exceed cap, with a monthly cost-to-complete review against the milestone calendar and early warning to MoDOT if any task threatens the cap. Cost reporting is aligned to the same line items used on the Price Page so invoices reconcile without rework.

component_records.title: Contract compliance, insurance and records obligations
component_records.description: A compliance lead carries the non-technical obligations: E-Verify enrollment affirmed by sworn affidavit with a completed Memorandum of Understanding, an affidavit that no unauthorized alien is knowingly employed, and lawful-presence proof for any sole proprietor or general partner. We provide certificates of insurance for general and automobile liability at $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence plus Missouri workers' compensation, flow Section (3) paragraph I provisions into every subcontract, and accept full liability for subcontractor performance. We obtain MHTC consent before any public release of materials or any assignment of interest, protect confidential factual matters and notify MHTC of any request for them, keep working papers available to MHTC and the State Auditor for three years after final payment, and comply with FFATA and 2 C.F.R. Part 170 reporting. We also pursue 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation.

items.text: The issuing body is the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), which is procuring the study on behalf of the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts.

MoDOT's Right of Way staff must produce property descriptions that accurately define land areas or rights to be acquired, conveyed or leased, reciting specific rights when less than fee simple title, and described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls.

Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.

Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, and a professional land surveyor must review the description before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the research.
The project is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that Division.
MoDOT's Research Director, Jen Harper, is designated as MHTC's representative for administering the Agreement and is the addressee for proposals and questions at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov.

The RFP is open to private consultants, universities and research organizations, and MoDOT is seeking proposer input on the best strategies to accomplish the research objectives rather than prescribing the method.

The goal is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for developing a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) using MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would then review and edit.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.

The work is organized into six tasks: Task 1 Project Management, Task 2 Literature Review, Task 3 (3a MoDOT-provided LLD examples, 3b Offeror names the program, 3c proof of concept), Task 4 Training and User Manual, Task 5 Draft Report and Research Summary, and Task 6 Final Report, Research Summary and Presentation.
Task 2 requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Task 3c requires a demonstration of how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and providing improvement feedback.
Task 4 requires the Offeror to train ROW staff on the finalized system and supply a user manual for staff reference.

Deliverables include a Data Management Plan due 12/4/2024, a draft final report, summary report and user manual due 11/3/2025, and a final report, summary report, presentation and user manual due 1/1/2026.

The Offeror must provide quarterly status meetings with minutes, quarterly written progress updates due the last working day of March, June, September and December, monthly e-mail and phone updates, and an interim presentation near the project mid-point (9/15/2025).

Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, and the cost estimate must be entered on the Section (4) Price Page with line items for Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, and Miscellaneous.
Proposals are due by 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024 to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.
Questions and comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and MoDOT posts its public responses on 7/31/2024.
MoDOT notifies submitters on 9/18/2024 whether the project is selected or whether interviews are needed to finalize selection.

After a responsiveness check, proposals are evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee, and the award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal; the RFP does not list the specific criteria or their weights.

The Work Plan must be a narrative of no more than ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, must cover all items in Section 2, and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans.

The proposal must be one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal (work plan and project schedule), Personnel, Organization's Project Experience, Team Member Experience, and Organization's Client References.

The proposal must identify experience delivering the requested services in the past three years and give the name, title and telephone number of at least three client officials from the past three years.

Any application must be built on approved technologies: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release (or .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), MVC, Razor Pages or Web API for web applications, and approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with large-scale Python use requiring BRPT approval.

Applications must be web-based, require no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), and meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508.

On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016 or higher only with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval), and no Personal Identifiable Information may be stored without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named LLD development program before Task 3c proof-of-concept work begins.

All documents, reports and exhibits produced at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties while auditing records for three years after final payment.

A Data Management Plan must be submitted within 2 weeks after the kick-off meeting, describing anticipated data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.

Offerors are encouraged to reach a target of 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation through subcontractors, suppliers or joint ventures, and the Offeror remains fully liable to MHTC for the quality and performance of subcontracted work.

Award requires an E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding and sworn affidavits under Section 285.530, RSMo. (Exhibit A), lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietors and general partners under Section 208.009, RSMo. (Exhibit B), and insurance of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence for general and automobile liability plus Missouri workers' compensation.

The bid team must obtain documents the RFP references but does not include: the Standard Research Agreement, the Proposal Submission Form, the Price Page template, the Publication Guidelines and research summary template, and the "Approved Technologies" section, all linked from https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.
MoDOT's Research Unit in the Construction and Materials Division coordinates the project and the Offeror must fully coordinate with that Division.
The RFP fixes the kick-off meeting at 11/15/2024 and the interim presentation at 9/15/2025.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named LLD development program before Task 3c proof-of-concept work begins.
MHTC realty rights must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must match the last deed of record.
Descriptions must meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 and be reviewed by a professional land surveyor before a deed is presented to the grantor.
Task 3a relies on LLD examples supplied by MoDOT as the input corpus.
The Data Management Plan is due 12/4/2024, two weeks after the 11/15/2024 kick-off meeting.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025 and the final versions 1/1/2026, with the final invoice due 2/2/2026.
Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.

Award requires an E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding, sworn affidavits under Sections 285.530 and 208.009 RSMo., and liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence.

The 15-month contract period is assumed to run from contract execution with the RFP milestone dates (11/15/2024 kick-off through 2/2/2026 final invoice) treated as fixed commitments, so the schedule is built backwards from those dates rather than from a negotiable start.

The named LLD development program is assumed to be approvable within roughly four to six weeks of submission, so the IS approval package is submitted immediately after kick-off to protect the 4/25/2025 proof-of-concept date.

The AI/ML drafting tool is assumed to be deployable on MoDOT-controlled infrastructure using the approved .NET and Oracle/SQL Server stack, with any cloud or third-party model service routed through BRPT and IS management review before use.

The MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 requirements are assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT at kick-off and to be the authoritative drafting rules encoded in the tool, with a professional land surveyor on the team validating output against them.

The Publication Guidelines and research summary template are assumed to be retrievable from the MoDOT information-for-researchers page before the draft report milestone, and report formatting is priced on that basis.

The Standard Research Agreement and the Price Page template are assumed to be obtainable from the MoDOT website and to match the terms summarized in the RFP, so pricing and contract review are scoped to those documents.

The volume of MoDOT-supplied LLD examples and the number of property types to be demonstrated in the proof of concept are assumed to be modest (on the order of a few dozen examples across several property types), which sets the evaluation and training effort within the $175,000 cap.

IS approval of the named LLD program gates the 4/25/2025 proof of concept. The RFP requires MoDOT Information Systems to approve the named LLD development program before any Task 3c proof-of-concept work, but states no approval criteria and no turnaround time. If approval takes longer than the assumed four to six weeks, or comes back with conditions (licensing, PII, hosting), the 4/25/2025 demonstration and every downstream milestone slip. The bidder carries the cost of idle specialist staff while waiting. The approval is a hard gate on the critical path with no stated criteria or service level, and the proposed solution itself assumes a four-to-six-week turnaround that the RFP does not promise. The proof-of-concept date is fixed at 4/25/2025, so any delay is unrecoverable within the 15-month term.

Deployment model for the AI/ML tool is undefined (on-premise vs cloud/SaaS). The RFP's technology rules describe on-premise .NET and Oracle/SQL Server deployments but never say whether the AI/ML drafting tool must run on MoDOT premises or may be a cloud or SaaS service. The proposed solution assumes MoDOT-controlled infrastructure with any third-party model service routed through BRPT review. If the client requires fully on-premise inference, the model choice, hardware and cost change materially; if a cloud model is permitted, the licensing and data-handling package changes instead. The RFP leaves the hosting question open while imposing approved-technology and no-PII constraints that a hosted model service may not satisfy. The design and price both turn on the answer, and the solution's assumption is an inference, not a stated client requirement.

MoDOT-supplied LLD example corpus may be larger or messier than assumed. The proof of concept, the evaluation and the training all rest on the LLD examples MoDOT supplies, and the solution assumes a few dozen examples across several property types. If the corpus is much larger, inconsistently formatted, or arrives late, the evaluation effort, the training data preparation and the accuracy claims all expand beyond what the $175,000 cap covers. Poor example quality would also depress measured accuracy and weaken the usefulness finding the study exists to produce. The volume and quality of the example corpus is an explicit assumption in the proposed solution, and the RFP does not commit to a size, format or delivery date. The corpus is the sole input to the proof of concept, so the assumption drives both schedule and price.

Fixed milestone calendar leaves no float for the IS approval and feedback loops. The RFP fixes the kick-off at 11/15/2024, the Data Management Plan at 12/4/2024, the demonstration at 4/25/2025, training at 7/25/2025, the interim presentation at 9/15/2025, the draft report at 11/3/2025 and the final deliverables at 1/1/2026. The solution builds the schedule backwards from these dates with no slack. Any single slip, particularly in the IS approval or in MoDOT's review-and-feedback cycle on the drafts, propagates to the final invoice date and puts the contract at risk. The milestone dates are contractual and the solution treats them as fixed commitments, with the approval gate and a client feedback loop both sitting on the critical path. The RFP does not say whether the dates are negotiable, so the bidder has no contractual relief for a slip.

Exhibits A and B are referenced but not provided. The RFP requires an E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding and sworn affidavits under Sections 285.530 and 208.009 RSMo., citing Exhibit A and Exhibit B as attached, but neither exhibit's content appears in the document. The bidder cannot confirm the exact affidavit wording, notarization or submission mechanics before the proposal deadline, and a defective affidavit is a responsiveness problem at award. Both exhibits are listed as referenced documents missing from the PDF, and the affidavits are mandatory award conditions. The content is standard state boilerplate, which limits the impact, but the omission is certain and must be resolved before submission.

EPG 236.4.6.2 drafting rules are not in the RFP. The tool must encode MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 and MHTC metes-and-bounds and deed-of-record rules, but the EPG section is not included in the RFP. The solution assumes it will be handed over at kick-off and is the authoritative rule set. If the rules are more intricate than assumed, or are applied with local variation by district, the rule encoding and surveyor validation effort grows and the accuracy demonstrated in the proof of concept suffers. The drafting rules are the core logic of the tool and the RFP does not provide them, so the effort estimate rests on an assumption. The consequence is rework of the rule engine and the evaluation, which contingency can absorb but which would consume schedule before the 4/25/2025 demonstration.

Pages 19 and 20 could not be read. Two pages of the RFP carry almost no extractable text and are dominated by images, so their content is unknown to the bid team. If they contain task detail, deliverable specifications or evaluation criteria, the proposal may miss a requirement or misprice the work. The risk is that a mandatory obligation sits on a page nobody could read. The pages fall in the task-description region of the RFP, where Task 3 through Task 6 detail is set out, so the missing content is likely substantive rather than decorative. The likelihood of a material omission depends on what the images show, which the bid team cannot currently tell.

Contract start date and 15-month term are inconsistent with the milestone table. The RFP says the contract period is 15 months and estimates a November 1, 2024 start, while the milestone table runs from a 11/15/2024 kick-off to a 2/2/2026 final invoice. If the contract is executed later than assumed, the fixed milestone dates compress the available period and the effort priced for 15 months has to be delivered in less. The bidder absorbs the compression. The RFP does not settle whether the 15 months runs from contract execution or from the kick-off meeting, and the solution assumes the milestone dates are fixed regardless. A late award or a slow contract execution is plausible given the 9/18/2024 notification date and the referenced but unavailable Standard Research Agreement.

Standard Research Agreement and Price Page template are not in the RFP. The contract that will govern the work, the Price Page template and the Proposal Submission Form are referenced on the MoDOT website but not included. The bidder prices and accepts terms it has not read, and a term in the Standard Research Agreement (indemnity, insurance, publication rights, payment) could require a change to the price or to the proposal after submission. The agreement governs the post-award relationship and is not available in the RFP, so the bid rests on an assumption that the summarized terms match the actual document. The Price Page template also determines how the cost estimate must be broken out, which affects the submission itself.

Accessibility conformance may require unplanned remediation of the drafting interface. The drafting environment must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508, including for the AI-generated draft review and edit screens. Accessibility is easy to underestimate in a data-dense editing interface, and remediation discovered late in the build would consume effort before the 7/25/2025 training date and the 1/1/2026 final deliverables. The requirement is explicit and the solution commits to it, but the RFP does not describe the accessibility testing or acceptance process, so the risk is that conformance is judged against an unstated bar. The impact is material rework of the interface, which contingency can absorb.

Publication Guidelines and research summary template are not provided. The draft and final reports must follow MoDOT's Publication Guidelines and research summary template, and the final report must carry a completed Technical Report Documentation page, but neither the guidelines nor the template is in the RFP. If the formatting requirements are more extensive than assumed, the report effort grows late in the schedule, when there is no float before the 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 dates. The formatting rules affect presentation rather than substance, so the impact is rework rather than failure, but the rework lands in the final two months of a schedule with no slack. The documents are referenced but absent, so the bid team cannot confirm the effort.

MBE/WBE participation targets may not be met within the cap. The RFP encourages 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation, and the Offeror remains fully liable for subcontracted work. On a $175,000 research engagement with a small core team, sourcing qualified MBE/WBE subcontractors for a narrow AI/ML and land-surveying scope may not be feasible without adding cost or management overhead, and the bidder carries the performance risk for any subcontractor it uses. The targets are encouraged rather than mandatory, so the impact is a weaker proposal rather than a failed one, but the narrow technical scope makes qualified participation genuinely uncertain. The bidder's full liability for subcontractor performance adds a management cost that the cap must absorb.
